sample.subject: Data Structures
sample.stem: Which data structure follows the LIFO (last in, first out) policy?
sample.a_reason: A queue does the opposite: it's FIFO, the first in is the first out.
sample.b_reason: The last in is the first out, like a stack of plates.
sample.c_reason: It allows inserting and removing at any position; it doesn't enforce LIFO.
sample.d_reason: It organises data as a hierarchy, not by order of arrival.

explain.label: Explanation
explain.xp: XP measures effort and only goes up: {{correct}} per correct answer, a bonus on harder questions and {{finish}} for finishing a session. Every {{level}} XP is a new level.
explain.rating: Rating is your level in each subject. Everyone starts at {{start}}; it goes up when you're right, down when you're wrong, and sets how hard your next questions are.
explain.streak: Your streak is the days in a row you've practiced. One finished session a day counts, even if you miss your goal.
explain.topics: The percentage is how often you get a topic right. At {{percent}}% correct over at least {{answers}} answers, it's mastered.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This page explains, in plain words, what data caramelCase keeps, what for, and how you control it.
privacy.who_body: caramelCase is run by [company name], [company registration number], [address]. To talk about privacy, write to [contact email]. Our data protection officer is [officer's name].
privacy.data_body:
- When you sign in: your email address and, if you use Google, the name Google gives us.
- Your preferences: language, timezone, theme, daily goal, and whether you want to see why each option is right or wrong.
- If you tell us: your university and course.
- Your practice: your sessions, each answer and how long it took, your rating, XP, streak and mastery of each topic.
- What you send us: your reports about questions, with any comment you write.
- App use: a few events, such as a visit to the front page.
- Technical logs: the IP address and time of each request to our server.

We keep no passwords: you sign in with Google or with a link sent by email.
privacy.use_body:
To run the app: picking questions at your level, counting your goal and streak, showing your progress and sending your sign-in link.

To improve the questions: your reports, and each question's success rate, which does not say who answered.

To protect the service: limiting repeated requests and looking into abuse.

We do not use your data for advertising, and we do not sell it.
privacy.device_body:
We use a single cookie, which keeps you signed in. It is not used for advertising or to follow you on other sites.

Your browser keeps your language, your theme and, if the connection drops during a session, the answer that has not been sent yet.

The app's fonts come from Google Fonts: to download them, your browser connects to Google's servers.
privacy.sharing_body:
- Google, if you sign in with Google: it tells us your email address and name.
- The service that sends our emails, which gets your address to send your sign-in link: [email provider].
- Our hosting, where the server and database run: [hosting provider], in [country].

Otherwise we only share data when the law requires it.
privacy.retention_body:
For as long as your account exists. When you delete your account, we erase your data and all your answers at once; our backups keep that data for up to 14 days.

Unused guest accounts: [period to be decided]. Technical logs: [period to be decided].
privacy.rights_body:
Brazil's data protection law (LGPD) lets you know what we keep, get a copy, correct it and erase it. In the app:

- Download your data: in Settings, “Download my data”.
- Erase everything: in Settings, “Delete account”.

To correct something, or for any other request, write to [contact email].
privacy.basis_body: [To be decided with legal counsel: the legal basis for each use of the data, such as providing the service you asked for by using the app.]
privacy.changes_body: When this policy changes, the new version appears here with its date. If the change is a big one, we will tell you in the app.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: By using caramelCase you agree to these terms. They are short on purpose.
terms.service_body:
caramelCase is an app for practising computer science with multiple-choice questions. The questions are written and checked with care, but they may contain mistakes: if you find one, use “Report question”.

The app helps you study. It does not replace your classes and does not guarantee exam results.
terms.account_body:
You can practise without signing up: the app creates a guest account on this device. When you sign in with Google or with an email link, your progress is kept in your account.

Look after access to your email: it is what lets you into your account.

[Minimum age to use the app: to be decided.]
terms.conduct_body:
- Do not copy the questions in bulk, by hand or with automated tools.
- Do not try to get into someone else's account or data.
- Do not overload the service or try to get around its limits.

We may suspend the account of anyone who does.
terms.content_body: The questions, explanations and the rest of the app's content belong to [company name]. You may use them for your own study; for any other use, ask us first.
terms.price_body: caramelCase is free today. If paid plans arrive, their terms will appear here before anyone is charged.
terms.liability_body: [To be decided with legal counsel: the availability of the service and the limits of liability.]
terms.ending_body: You can delete your account whenever you like, in Settings. If caramelCase shuts down, we will tell you [notice period] in advance.
terms.law_body: These terms follow Brazilian law. Disputes go to the courts of [city/state].
